# My plan for this year

I'm 45, been farming this land for 20 years. My boy is still in school and my wife helps in the field when she can — that's really just two pairs of hands most days, plus hired help when the cotton and stevia need picking. 58 mu is not small, not big. I can't afford to waste money on inputs, but I'm not scraping by either.

Here's how I'm splitting the land this season:

- **Stevia: 20 mu.** This is my main money crop now. The buyer comes from the contract company and picks up dried leaves. Price is better than grain but the work is heavy — transplanting seedlings, weeding by hand because the chemicals will ruin the leaf quality, and two or three cuttings over the summer. I've been growing stevia for about 6 years now and I know the rhythm. I put on more fertilizer here than on wheat because the buyer pays for leaf weight.
- **Wheat–maize double cropping: 25 mu.** This is the insurance. Even if stevia price drops or cotton gets hit by something, we eat and the flour is there. The rotation is what my father did and his father before him. Wheat in October after I clear the maize, maize mid-June right after the wheat combine comes through.
- **Cotton: 13 mu.** I keep cotton on the sandier ground on the west side where wheat doesn't do as well. Bt seed so I don't spray for bollworm like the old days, but aphids and spider mites still come and I have to watch. Cotton pays okay if the weather holds, and picking gives my wife's cousins some work in the fall.

## How I'm thinking about each crop

**Wheat.** I plant around October 10th-15th, depends on when the ground is ready after maize. I buy improved seed from the agri-supply shop in town, about 12-13 kg per mu — I know the extension guy says 10 is enough but thinner stands worry me if the winter is dry. For fertilizer, I put down a compound fertilizer (triple-15 type) before planting, maybe 40 kg per mu, then topdress urea at jointing in early March — about 20 kg. That works out to around 17 kg N per mu total, which is a little more than the extension station recommends but my yields have been steady so I'm not changing. I irrigate before the ground freezes in December, then at jointing, then once more at grain filling if the spring rain is short. The well is metered and pumping costs me maybe 15 yuan per mu per time so I don't irrigate more than I need.

**Summer maize.** Straight after wheat, no tillage — the no-till seeder goes right through the stubble. I hire that because I don't own the machine, costs me about 30 yuan per mu. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan 958 or whatever is the popular variety that year, about 2.5 kg per mu. Fertilizer is lighter because I just fertilized wheat and the residue helps — maybe 12 kg N per mu at the V6 stage as one side-dress with urea. One irrigation at tasseling if July is dry. Spray herbicide once after emergence for broadleaves.

**Cotton.** Plant mid-April when the soil temperature comes up, around the 20th. I deep plow the cotton fields in March, that's the difference — cotton wants loose soil. Seed about 1 kg per mu of Bt variety. Base fertilizer heavy — compound plus some urea, around 14 kg N per mu total. I irrigate twice, once at squaring and once at boll-setting. Pesticide is the tricky part — even with Bt cotton I still spray maybe 3-4 times through the season for aphids, mites, and mirid bugs. That adds up, maybe 120 yuan per mu in chemicals.

**Stevia.** This is where I spend the most per mu. Transplant seedlings in late April — I buy them from the cooperative, about 400 yuan per mu for the plants. Before transplanting I put down organic fertilizer (chicken manure, maybe 500 kg per mu) plus compound fertilizer. After the first cutting in July I topdress urea. Total N is maybe 20 kg per mu. Irrigation is critical — stevia doesn't like drought, so 4-5 times through the summer. Weeding is all by hand with hired day labor, that's the biggest cost. Two cuttings usually, sometimes a third if the weather's good and the first cut comes early.

I'm budgeting around 37,000-40,000 yuan for inputs this year. If the stevia contract price holds at last year's level, I should clear decent money. If cotton has a bad year I still have the wheat-maize to fall back on. That's how it works.
